newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Market economy needed for Ethiopia -- PM says.
newsitem.headline: Market economy needed for Ethiopia -- PM says.

text.p: Ethiopian Prime Minister Meles Zenawi said on Saturday that the only way to end poverty in the Horn of Africa country was to strictly adhere to basic market principles.

"Ethiopia could ensure its survival only when it succeeded in creating economic institutions capable of competing in the world market, because competitivness is one of the most important dictates of current international order," Meles said at a news conference.
A decision this month to end subsidised fuel and rent on state-owned houses in the captial Addis Ababa touched off protests by businesses.
The state-run Ethiopian News Agency (ENA) quoted him as saying such measures were necessary for a free market to develop.
Meles said that with a free market, Ethiopia could boost its grain production and could become food self-sufficient within a year.
Meles, whose guerrilla forces overthrew Marxist Dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam in 1991, launched a liberal economic policy in 1992.
